Because the interface is graphical, it also works as a genuine teaching tool, letting students explore the fundamental building blocks of pulse sequences without needing to learn a coding language first.

sections.title: Building a Custom Pulse Sequence
body: Writing a custom pulse sequence sounds like it should require a programming background. Experiment Designer is built specifically so it doesn't.

The workflow runs in three clear steps. First, the SeqDev platform opens for editing or creating a pulse sequence, with elements like channels, pulses, and delays added to the diagram with a double-click. Second, once the sequence is complete, it's exported as an application, carrying along any pre-acquisition settings such as automatic Receiver Gain calculation, so the experiment doesn't need to be reconfigured every time it runs. Third, that application loads directly into NMRGUI, the instrument's onboard software, ready to run. Acquisition parameters can be defined in advance for routine use, while still leaving room for fine-tuning when a specific run calls for it.

sections.title: Teaching NMR Fundamentals Through SeqDev
body: Understanding what a pulse sequence actually does is different from just running one. SeqDev's graphical design makes that understanding accessible without a coding prerequisite standing in the way.

Because sequence elements are placed visually, on a diagram, with a double-click, rather than typed as code, students can explore what each channel, pulse, and delay contributes to an experiment directly. That turns Experiment Designer into more than an expert tool. It becomes a way to teach the fundamental principles of NMR pulse sequence design hands-on, letting students build understanding piece by piece rather than treating the sequence as a black box.

sections.title: Controlling Your Instrument From Anywhere
body: A lab rarely works the way a product photo suggests, with one person standing at one instrument for the length of a run. Remote Access is built around that reality.

Once enabled, it extends control of your Nanalysis benchtop NMR beyond the instrument itself, to whatever device is already in your hand, a PC at your desk, a phone in your pocket, or a tablet you're carrying between rooms. That means checking on a run, adjusting something, or simply confirming things are on track doesn't require walking back to the bench every time.
